events.instrument: Ley 21.542, modifica la Carta Fundamental con el objeto de permitir la protección de infraestructura crítica por parte de las Fuerzas Armadas
events.article: Constitución Art. 32 Nº 21 (last paragraph) and 53rd transitory provision
events.what_changed: Allows the President to deploy the Armed Forces to guard border-zone areas, subject to rules on the use of force, and authorises a DFL setting their powers. It authorises force at the border; it does not prohibit it.
events.passage: La atribución especial contenida en este numeral también se podrá utilizar para el resguardo de áreas de las zonas fronterizas del país, de acuerdo a las instrucciones contenidas en el decreto supremo que se dicte en conformidad con la ley.

events.instrument: Decreto con Fuerza de Ley Núm. 1, de 2023, para el resguardo de las áreas de zonas fronterizas
events.what_changed: Gives the forces guarding border zones powers to check identity and to detain people entering through unauthorised crossings, and sets use-of-force principles and a graduated 10-rule scale (dissuasion, non-lethal weapons, riot weapons, firearms as a last resort). Force is regulated and allowed when necessary to guard the border, not prohibited, so the q9 answer stays No.
events.passage: b) Principio de necesidad: En el cumplimiento del deber de velar por el resguardo de las Áreas de zonas fronterizas se puede utilizar la fuerza solo cuando sea estrictamente necesaria para cumplir el deber.

events.what_changed: Widens immediate reconducción (return) to people caught entering while evading control, or found up to 10 km inside the land border. It says nothing about force, so it leaves the indicator unchanged.
events.passage: o que se haya internado al territorio nacional hasta 10 kilómetros del límite fronterizo terrestre o dentro del mar territorial, ... será inmediatamente reembarcado o reconducido a la frontera

events.what_changed: A soldier used a riot shotgun (non-lethal) against six migrants trying to cross by an unauthorised route; the Defence Minister described this as preventing an irregular entry. It shows force being used to stop entry, which the law permits.
events.passage: al verse amenazado, utilizó armamento no letal, una escopeta antidisturbios, haciendo que los migrantes regresaran a territorio boliviano

answers.implementation_then_now: Does Not Apply on both dates: no law prohibits the use of force to prevent entry. Since February 2023, DFL 1/2023 expressly authorises the forces guarding the border to use graduated force. Press reports from 2024–2025 show soldiers using force at Colchane to stop entries: shots at a van carrying 17 migrants in February 2024, and a riot shotgun used in October 2025.

events.what_changed: For the forces guarding the border and controlling entry, firearms are allowed only as a last resort against people using or about to use lethal weapons, or otherwise endangering life. Lethal force is therefore excluded as a means of stopping entry as such. Before this, no rule specific to entry existed (starting answer No).

events.what_changed: Soldiers fired two shots at a van carrying 17 irregular migrants that evaded a checkpoint, hitting the bumper and a wheel; no one was injured. The regional delegate justified it as a risk to the soldiers. This is the one documented use of firearms in the context of entry.
events.passage: el personal militar del lugar realizó dos disparos contra el vehículo. Uno de ellos dio en el parachoque y otro en la rueda delantera. ... no reportaron personas heridas.

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: Does Not Apply (starting answer No). 2026: Usually. DFL 1/2023 confines firearms to threats to life, and the reporting I found shows mostly non-lethal force at the border. In October 2025 the army used a riot shotgun and reported acting under its use-of-force rules. The one firearm incident found, in February 2024, was two shots at an evading van carrying migrants; no one was injured, and the authorities justified it as a risk to the soldiers. I found no reported deaths of migrants from state force at the border. The evidence is press reporting about irregular migrants at the northern border, not monitoring-body findings.

answers.starting_answer_concern: Chile already had police use-of-force rules before 2023 (Decreto 1.364 of 2018 and Carabineros Circular 1.832). Under the MRD's Peru example, firearm-restriction rules can support a 'Yes'. I did not read those texts, so I keep the starting 'No' for 2023; a reviewer may want to check them.
answers.notes: The change rests on DFL 1/2023, a decree with force of law (Rule 8). Its wording is equivalent to the Peruvian Decreto Legislativo 1186 Art. 8.3 that the MRD coded 'Yes'. Its scope is limited to the forces deployed to guard border-zone areas under the constitutional mechanism, which is the situation this indicator asks about. Ley 21.849 (Reglas del Uso de la Fuerza, published 2026-10-16) falls after the window; I did not read it.

answers.answer_2023: Yes, the national law provides exemption
answers.answer_2026: Yes, the national law provides exemption
answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

events.what_changed: Rewords the authorisation of interception and special investigative techniques in trafficking and smuggling investigations. It does not touch the treatment of victims or smuggled migrants.
events.passage: Ley 21577 Art. 1 Nº 11 a) y b) D.O. 15.06.2023 ... Cuando existan fundadas sospechas de que una persona ha cometido o preparado la comisión de alguno de los delitos indicados en este Párrafo

events.what_changed: Art. 411 sexies, which allowed a sentence reduction of two degrees for offenders who cooperate effectively, was repealed (general cooperation rules were moved to the Código Procesal Penal). It never concerned non-punishment of victims or smuggled migrants, so the indicator is not affected.

answers.implementation_then_now: Usually on both dates. The US TIP Report 2022 (covering 2021–22) found no pattern of victims being penalised, but recommended guidelines so that children are not penalised for acts traffickers compelled. It also noted that the 2021 migration law expressly prohibits deporting identified trafficking victims. The TIP Report 2025 (covering 2024) keeps Chile at Tier 1 and reports the deportation bar and victim visas (18 in 2023, 3 in 2024). It again urges active screening of vulnerable migrants, which points to identification gaps rather than prosecution of victims. For smuggled migrants, Ley 21.325 Art. 9 states that irregular migration is not a crime; their exposure is administrative (reconducción was widened by Ley 21.655 in 2024), not criminal.

answers.sourcing_note: I read the Código Penal version of 2023-01-01 and the current version on LeyChile, which carry amendment markers for Ley 21.523 (31.12.2022, before the window), Ley 21.577 (2023) and Ley 21.694 (2024). Código Procesal Penal Art. 78 bis and Ley 21.325 Arts. 7, 9 and 13 show no amendments in the window. I did not open Decreto 42/2005.
answers.starting_answer_concern: None of the cited provisions contains an express non-punishment clause. Art. 411 bis punishes only the smuggler. CPP Art. 78 bis provides protection measures during the criminal process. Ley 21.325 Arts. 7 and 13 promote regularisation and allow a visa for trafficking victims. The strongest basis for smuggled migrants is Ley 21.325 Art. 9 ('La migración irregular no es constitutiva de delito'), which the starting answer does not cite. For trafficked persons who commit offences under compulsion, there is no specific exemption; the 2022 TIP Report recommended guidelines to ensure such victims are not penalised. On a strict reading, the 'Yes' is doubtful. It is kept here because nothing changed in the window.
answers.notes: Practice evidence comes from US TIP reports, which cover trafficking victims (mostly identified victims) more than smuggled migrants. No change in law or practice was found in the window that bears on non-punishment.
